focus: Measurement trustworthiness: frame dependence, oracle dropouts, contested labels

title: Keep survives only against the structurally blind baseline; vs constant-same or lexical zero-call rules the Keep Rule prints stop (margin).
Four of 60 labeled pairs are oracle-undecidable, all labeled same and all called same by Jev; the scorer counts them as baseline misses.
Eight of the twelve different labels are bare dimension-name pairs from one review run, so specificity is earned mostly on trivial pairs.
Three different labels are near-verbatim restatements that the model confidently called same; a relabel would move the column to 56/60, and the gold-versus-question contract is untested.
The report records no label digest, labeler or per-pair oracle decision; requalify pins the model but not the gold.
The pair sheet refuses in-repo paths by design, so the census is reproducible in-tree while the verdict is not; the pair universe is commit-scoped through git ls-files.

A trustworthy protocol is assembly not machinery: pre-registered baselines, a second rater on the different class, class stratification, label digest and per-pair decisions, and an oracle-dropout bucket.
